sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test tool and benchmark imports
sections.what: Brings in the test tool's grouping and checking helpers, and the benchmark functions the tests need.
sections.why: The tests need these tools to run and to call the benchmark code.
sections.watch_out: Renaming an imported function will break every test that uses it.

sections.name: synthetic evaluation benchmark
sections.title: Benchmark tests
sections.what: Runs four checks: the case list has twelve synthetic cases with the expected ground truth, the production check gives the expected result for a clean case and twenty-four rule checks, the scores are correct when outcomes are wrong, and wording with a forbidden claim is caught while safe wording passes.
sections.why: Each test protects a different part of the accuracy claim, so a mistake in one area shows up clearly.
sections.watch_out: Tests pin exact numbers. If the benchmark cases change on purpose, these numbers must be updated too.

summary: Automatic tests that check the benchmark cases, the scoring rules and the prohibited-claim check still behave as expected.
purpose: Guards the evaluation so a change to the checks does not quietly change the reported accuracy or let risky wording through.
why: Tests lock in the expected results so regressions are caught early. Likely reason: the app reports accuracy to users, so it must not drift. Reason not stated in the code.
how: The file imports the test tool and the benchmark helpers, then runs four tests: the case list is correct, the production check gives the expected results, the scores are computed from real outcomes, and prohibited wording is caught.
inputs: The benchmark cases and helper functions from the benchmark module.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each test.
risks: A test that hard-codes counts, such as twelve cases or twenty-four checks, will fail whenever those numbers are intentionally changed.
debug: If a test fails, read the expected and actual values in the failure message, then compare the matching case in the benchmark module.
